id: The Men That Don't Fit In

prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

There's a race of men that don't fit in, A race that can't stay still; So they break the hearts of kith and kin, And they roam the world at will. They range the field and they rove the flood, And they climb the mountain's crest; Theirs is the curse of the gypsy blood, And they don't know how to rest.If they just went straight they might go far; They are strong and brave and true; But they're always tired of the things that are, And they want the strange and new. They say: "Could I find my proper groove, What a deep mark I would make!" So they chop and change, and each fresh move Is only a fresh mistake. And each forgets, as he strips and runs With a brilliant, fitful pace, It's the steady, quiet, plodding ones Who win in the lifelong race. And each forgets that his youth has fled, Forgets that his prime is past, Till he stands one day, with a hope that's dead, In the glare of the truth at last. He has failed, he has failed; he has missed his chance; He has just done things by half. Life's been a jolly good joke on him, And now is the time to laugh. Ha, ha! He is one of the Legion Lost; He was never meant to win; He's a rolling stone, and it's bred in the bone; He's a man who won't fit in.

prompts.L3:
Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

- Some people are driven by an innate restlessness that prevents them from settling down or fitting into conventional life.
- Although they are strong, brave, and capable, they continually abandon the familiar in pursuit of something new.
- Their constant changes and search for the perfect path lead to repeated mistakes and unfinished efforts.
- They overlook that steady, persistent people are more likely to succeed over the course of a lifetime.
- By the time they recognize their wasted potential and missed opportunities, their youth and best chances have passed.
prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

The poem explores restless people who never fit in, portraying their lifelong roaming and constant pursuit of novelty through vivid contrasts with steady, persevering individuals. It concludes that their repeated changes and half-finished efforts lead to wasted potential and failure, warning that persistence—not brilliance without commitment—wins life’s race.

Keywords: There, And, They

outputs.L1:
There is a race of men who do not fit in,  
A race that cannot stay still;  
So they break the hearts of kith and kin,  
And roam the world at will.  
They range the fields and rove the floods,  
And climb to the mountain’s crest;  
Theirs is the curse of gypsy blood,  
And they do not know how to rest.

If only they went straight, they might go far;  
They are strong and brave and true.  
But they are always weary of things as they are,  
And forever seek the strange and new.  
They say, “Could I but find my proper groove,  
What a lasting mark I would make!”  
So they chop and change, and each fresh move  
Becomes yet another mistake.

And each forgets, as he strips and runs  
With a brilliant, fitful pace,  
That the steady, quiet, plodding ones  
Are those who win the lifelong race.  
And each forgets that his youth has fled,  
Forgets that his prime is past,  
Until one day he stands, his hope now dead,  
In the glare of truth at last.

He has failed—he has failed; he has missed his chance;  
He has done all things by half.  
Life has played a jolly good joke on him,  
And now is the time to laugh.  
Ha, ha! He is one of the Legion Lost;  
He was never meant to win.  
He is a rolling stone—it is bred in the bone—  
He is a man who will not fit in.
outputs.L2:
Some men seem incapable of belonging anywhere or remaining in one place. Driven by an inborn restlessness, they leave sorrow behind among friends and relatives while wandering wherever they please. They cross open country and oceans and scale the highest peaks, cursed with a nomadic spirit that never allows them peace.

With their strength, courage, and honesty, they could accomplish much if only they followed a consistent course. Instead, familiar circumstances quickly bore them, and they continually seek whatever is unfamiliar and different. Each imagines that, if he could only discover the role that truly suited him, he would achieve something remarkable. Yet he repeatedly changes his plans, and every new beginning becomes another error.

Rushing forward in dazzling but irregular bursts, he fails to recognize that life’s long contest is ultimately won by patient, unassuming people who keep working steadily. He also ignores the passing of time, not noticing that his youth is gone and his finest years are behind him. Eventually, he must face the harsh truth when all his hopes have died.

By then, he understands that he has not succeeded. He let his opportunity slip away because he never completed anything wholeheartedly. Life has played an excellent joke on him, and at last comes the moment for laughter: ha, ha! He belongs among the great company of the lost, never destined for victory. He is forever a rolling stone, restless by nature—a man who can never fit in.
outputs.L3:
Some people are driven by an innate restlessness that makes it difficult for them to settle down or adapt to the expectations of conventional life. They may possess great strength, courage, intelligence, and ability, yet they repeatedly abandon familiar surroundings and established paths in pursuit of something new. Each fresh beginning promises fulfillment, but their constant changes of direction often lead them to repeat the same mistakes, leave worthwhile efforts unfinished, and waste opportunities that might have produced lasting results.

What they fail to recognize is that success is not always achieved by the most talented or adventurous individuals. More often, it belongs to those who remain steady, patient, and persistent—people who continue working toward their goals despite boredom, difficulty, or uncertainty. Over the course of a lifetime, consistency can accomplish more than bursts of enthusiasm followed by retreat. Unfortunately, restless individuals may understand this lesson only when it is too late. By the time they become aware of their wasted potential and the opportunities they have allowed to slip away, their youth has faded and many of their best chances have already passed.
outputs.L4:
The poem focuses on restless, dissatisfied people who never feel at home in one place or committed to one purpose. Driven by a constant desire for novelty, they move from place to place, abandon one ambition for another, and repeatedly change their plans whenever the first excitement begins to fade. Although they may possess intelligence, energy, and natural talent, they lack the patience needed to turn those qualities into lasting achievement. Their lives become a series of fresh beginnings rather than a record of completed work.

The poet contrasts these wanderers with steady and persevering individuals. Such people may appear less brilliant or adventurous, but they remain loyal to their chosen path and continue working through boredom, hardship, and disappointment. While the restless person is attracted by every new possibility, the persistent person understands that meaningful success usually comes through discipline, endurance, and sustained effort. The contrast shows that determination can accomplish more than talent that is constantly redirected.

As the poem develops, the restless characters’ freedom begins to look less like independence and more like aimlessness. Each change wastes time and leaves another task unfinished. Because they never stay with anything long enough to master it, their abilities remain undeveloped and their promise is never fulfilled. Their pursuit of novelty ultimately produces frustration and failure rather than satisfaction.

The poem therefore offers a clear warning about the dangers of inconsistency. Brilliance, enthusiasm, and ambition are not enough if they are not supported by commitment. A person who repeatedly changes direction may expend enormous energy without making real progress, whereas someone who advances patiently and steadily is far more likely to succeed. In life’s race, the poem concludes, persistence and perseverance triumph over talent without purpose.

counterfactuals.output:
## “The Men That Don’t Fit In”  
*by Robert W. Service*

There’s a race of men that don’t fit in,  
A race that can’t stay still;  
So they break the hearts of kith and kin,  
And they roam the world at will.  
They range the field and they rove the flood,  
And they climb the mountain’s crest;  
Theirs is the curse of the gypsy blood,  
And they don’t know how to rest.

If they just went straight they might go far;  
They are strong and brave and true;  
But they’re always tired of the things that are,  
And they want the strange and new.  
They say: “Could I find my proper groove,  
What a deep mark I would make!”  
So they chop and change, and each fresh move  
Is only a fresh mistake.

And each forgets, as he strips and runs  
With a brilliant, fitful pace,  
It’s the steady, quiet, plodding ones  
Who win in the lifelong race.  
And each forgets that his youth has fled,  
Forgets that his prime is past,  
Till he stands one day, with a hope that’s dead,  
In the glare of the truth at last.

He has failed, he has failed; he has missed his chance;  
He has just done things by half.  
Life’s been a jolly good joke on him,  
And now is the time to laugh.  
Ha, ha! He is one of the Legion Lost;  
He was never meant to win;  
He’s a rolling stone, and it’s bred in the bone;  
He’s a man who won’t fit in.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1
